Infer a reproduction matrix from sufficient statistics

Source: R/inference.R
infer_R_sufficient.Rd

Fits the independent Poisson transmission model in Eqs. (27)–(30) of Wang and Valdano (2026). S[i, j] is the total number of observed transmissions from source j to destination i, and E[j] is the total number of infectious source-j individuals exposed across the preceding generations. Rows are destinations and columns are sources.

Usage

infer_R_sufficient(
  S,
  E,
  prior_shape = NULL,
  prior_rate = NULL,
  structural_zero = NULL
)

Arguments

S

A finite nonnegative square numeric matrix of integer transmission counts. Row and column identifiers must be unique and identical in the same order.

E

A named finite nonnegative numeric vector of integer source exposures, in the same order as the columns of S.

prior_shape

A required finite positive scalar or matrix of Gamma prior shape parameters.

prior_rate

A required finite positive scalar or matrix of Gamma prior rate parameters.

structural_zero

Optional logical matrix identifying edges fixed at zero by design. Positive observations on those edges are rejected. A zero observed count is otherwise treated as a sampling zero, not a structural zero.

Value

An object of class routbreak_inference containing sufficient statistics S and E; square destination-by-source matrices mle, status, prior_shape, prior_rate, alpha_post, beta_post, posterior_mean, and posterior_variance; the logical matrix structural_zero; and model metadata. The mle is NA for unidentified zero-exposure entries, while their proper-prior posterior moments remain defined. Declared structural zeros have zero MLE and posterior moments.

Details

The maximum-likelihood estimate is S[i, j] / E[j] when E[j] > 0. Entries with zero exposure are reported as unidentified rather than set to zero. Under a proper Gamma prior in shape-rate form, posterior shape is prior_shape + S and posterior rate is prior_rate + E[j].

Prior parameters are required explicitly because a fixed independent prior on every edge implies a different prior for total reproduction as the number of communities changes. For example, if every edge has a common Gamma(a, b) prior, the prior mean of each source-column total is n * a / b. Users should elicit priors for the matrix scale and structure relevant to their study. This is not the paper's improper flat-prior construction. The posterior mean is (prior_shape + S) / (prior_rate + E), whereas the MLE remains S / E.

Examples

ids <- c("A", "B")
S <- matrix(c(12, 4, 3, 16), 2, byrow = TRUE,
            dimnames = list(ids, ids))
fit <- infer_R_sufficient(
  S, E = c(A = 10, B = 20), prior_shape = 1, prior_rate = 1
)
fit$mle
#>     A   B
#> A 1.2 0.2
#> B 0.3 0.8
fit$posterior_mean
#>           A         B
#> A 1.1818182 0.2380952
#> B 0.3636364 0.8095238
